title: Mycelial Path Of Least Action
definition: A fundamental principle stating that complex systems evolve toward the most immediately accessible stable state, often at the cost of long-term potential.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine a ball rolling down a hill. It will go to the lowest point it can, even if it's not the best long-term choice. This rule explains why we make poor decisions under stress and why ecosystems collapse.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: This principle, also known as the 'path of least action', is a fundamental concept in physics. It describes how a system will evolve when perturbed. This dynamic often leads to a loss of complexity and resilience, manifesting as 'futile cycles' and systemic collapse.
difficulty_levels.expert: The 'Mycelial Path of Least Action' is a broad, philosophical concept connecting physics, thermodynamics, and systems theory. It describes the universal trade-off between short-term stability and long-term potential. This principle has profound implications for understanding complexity, resilience, and the fundamental nature of reality. It also highlights the role of consciousness as the only known exception to this rule.

extra_fields.insight: The universe consistently trades long-term potential for short-term stability, creating a cycle of futility and collapse.
